title: Local stalk model at a valuation special-fibre component generic point
statement: Let $A$ be a valuation domain (an integral domain such that each nonzero element of its fraction field or its inverse belongs to $A$), with fraction field $K$, maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$, residue field $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $f:X\to S$ be locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent finite type $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Write $t,s\in S$ for its generic and closed points. Let $y\in X_t$, let $Y=\overline{\{y\}}$ with reduced induced integral closed-subscheme structure [def-pc-integral-scheme; lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], and let $x$ be a generic point [def-sc-generic-point] of an irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $Y_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Regard $x,y$ as points of $X$, put $B=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $N=\mathcal F_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], and let $\mathfrak q\subseteq B$ be the prime corresponding to the generalization $y$ of $x$. Then $A\to B$ is a local homomorphism essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], $N$ is finite [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], $\mathfrak q\cap A=(0)$, and $\sqrt{\mathfrak q+\mathfrak m_AB}=\mathfrak m_B$. Here $\sqrt I=\{b\mid b^n\in I\text{ for some }n\geq1\}$. Put $B_K=B\otimes_AK$, $N_K=N\otimes_AK$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], $\mathfrak q_K=\mathfrak qB_K$, $R=B/\mathfrak m_AB$, $L=N/\mathfrak m_AN$, $T=(B_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}$ and $P=(N_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Writing $\mathcal F_r=i_r^*\mathcal F$ on $X_r$ for $r=s,t$ [def-pc-module-pullback], there are canonical compatible ring and module identifications $R\cong\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$, $L\cong(\mathcal F_s)_x$, $T\cong\mathcal O_{X_t,y}$ and $P\cong(\mathcal F_t)_y$. The ring $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $L$ is finite over $R$. Under these identifications, $x\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal F)$ if and only if $\mathfrak m_R\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(L)$, and $y\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal F)$ if and only if $\mathfrak m_T\in\operatorname{Ass}_T(P)$ [def-trf-relative-assassin; def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes].

source.place: Tag 0GSI (lemma-associated-point-specializes), third proof paragraph: A to B, the closed-fibre stalk quotients, the prime q and its radical condition, and the two generic-fibre stalk localizations.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}C$ of $x$ with $C$ a finite type $A$-algebra, using the affine cover in the definition of locally finite type. Write $\mathfrak p\subset C$ for $x$. The affine stalk comparison gives $B=C_{\mathfrak p}$, so $A\to B$ is essentially of finite type by its definition. Since $f(x)=s$, the stalk map is local; its source is $\mathcal O_{S,s}=A_{\mathfrak m_A}=A$ (elements outside $\mathfrak m_A$ are already units). The finite-type module stalk lemma gives that $N=\mathcal F_x$ is finite over $B$.

source.place: Tag 0GSI (lemma-associated-point-specializes), third proof paragraph, local ring and module setup; schemes.tex Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), part (6).

proof.text: Because $x\in\overline{\{y\}}$, every open containing $x$ contains $y$; in particular $y\in U$. Let $\mathfrak q_0\subset C$ represent $y$. Then $\mathfrak q_0\subseteq\mathfrak p$: if $c\in\mathfrak q_0\setminus\mathfrak p$, the open $D(c)$ would contain $x$ but not $y$. The localization-spectrum embedding gives the unique prime $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak q_0C_{\mathfrak p}$ of $B$ corresponding to $y$. The canonical local-spectrum morphism identifies it with the generalization in the statement. Its contraction to $A$ is zero, because its contraction to $C$ is $\mathfrak q_0$ and the image of $y$ in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is the prime $(0)$.

source.place: Tag 01J7 (lemma-specialize-points), proof, and Tag 01J6 (lemma-morphism-from-spec-local-ring); algebra.tex Tag 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization).

proof.text: Apply the fibre-stalk quotient lemma to $f$ at $x$, using $\mathcal O_{S,s}=A$. It gives the canonical isomorphism $R=B/\mathfrak m_AB\cong\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ induced by the fibre projection $i_s$. The pullback-stalk lemma then gives $(i_s^*\mathcal F)_x\cong N\otimes_B R$. The quotient-tensor isomorphism (with the symmetry of tensor products) identifies this with $L=N/\mathfrak m_AN$, sending the class of a germ $n$ to $n\otimes1$. Thus the ring and module comparisons are compatible with scalar multiplication and the pullback of germs. No flatness of $\mathcal F$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0GSI (lemma-associated-point-specializes), third proof paragraph, closed-fibre stalks; schemes.tex Tag 0HA1 (lemma-local-ring-fibre), sheaves.tex Tag 0098 (lemma-stalk-pullback-modules), algebra.tex Tag 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact).

proof.text: The local essentially finite type map of step 1 satisfies the hypotheses of the valuation closed-fibre Noetherian lemma, so $R$ is Noetherian. If $n_1,\ldots,n_d$ generate $N$ over $B$, their classes generate $L$ over $R$: the equality $n=\sum b_i n_i$ passes to $\bar n=\sum\bar b_i\bar n_i$. Hence $L$ is finite over $R$, including when $N=0$.

source.place: Tag 0GSG (lemma-mod-injective-valuation-ring), second proof paragraph, Noetherianity of the closed-fibre ring and finiteness of the quotient module.

proof.text: In $U$, the closure of $y$ is $V(\mathfrak q_0)$: it is the smallest closed set containing $\mathfrak q_0$, since $\mathfrak q_0\in V(J)$ means $J\subseteq\mathfrak q_0$. The reduced induced structure therefore identifies $Y\cap U$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(C/\mathfrak q_0)$. The affine fibre-product and quotient-tensor formulas identify its special fibre with $\operatorname{Spec}(C/I)$, where $I=\mathfrak q_0+\mathfrak m_AC$. The component of $Y_s$ with generic point $x$ remains a component after intersection with this open: an irreducible closed set in the open strictly containing that intersection would have irreducible closure in $Y_s$ strictly containing the original component. The spectrum-component/minimal-prime correspondence, applied to $C/I$, now says that $\mathfrak p$ is minimal over $I$. The minimal-prime localization radical lemma gives $\sqrt{IC_{\mathfrak p}}=\mathfrak pC_{\mathfrak p}$. Since $IC_{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak q+\mathfrak m_AB$ and $\mathfrak pC_{\mathfrak p}=\mathfrak m_B$, this is the required radical equality.

source.place: Tag 0GSI (lemma-associated-point-specializes), third proof paragraph, radical assertion; schemes.tex Tags 01J3 (lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); algebra.tex Tag 00ES (lemma-irreducible), part (3).

proof.text: Put $M=\mathcal F(U)$. The affine module germ-localization lemma identifies $N$ with $M_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathcal F_y$ with $M_{\mathfrak q_0}$, compatibly with the ring germ localizations $C_{\mathfrak p}=B$ and $C_{\mathfrak q_0}=\mathcal O_{X,y}$. Localizing again at $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak q_0B$ gives $B_{\mathfrak q}\cong C_{\mathfrak q_0}$ and $N_{\mathfrak q}\cong M_{\mathfrak q_0}$. Explicitly the ring comparison sends $(c/u)/(d/v)$ to $cv/(ud)$, and the module comparison sends $(m/u)/(d/v)$ to $vm/(ud)$, where $u,v\notin\mathfrak p$ and $d\notin\mathfrak q_0$. Inverses send $c/d$ and $m/d$ to $(c/1)/(d/1)$ and $(m/1)/(d/1)$. The fraction equivalence relation verifies that these maps are well-defined and inverse; both send germs to the corresponding fractions. Thus $\mathcal O_{X,y}=B_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\mathcal F_y=N_{\mathfrak q}$ with compatible scalars.

source.place: Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), parts (6),(7), and Tag 01IB (lemma-quasi-coherent-affine-equivalence); algebra.tex Tag 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization).

proof.text: Set $S=A\setminus\{0\}$. Since $K=S^{-1}A$, localization over the base identifies $B_K$ with $S^{-1}B$ and $N_K$ with $S^{-1}N$ (apply the cited tensor-localization lemma with intermediate algebra $A$, module $A$, and second module $B$ or $N$, then use tensor symmetry). By $\mathfrak q\cap A=0$, the images of $S$ avoid $\mathfrak q$, so the spectrum-localization correspondence makes $\mathfrak q_K=S^{-1}\mathfrak q$ prime. Localizing at it inverts exactly the elements needed for $B_{\mathfrak q}$. The canonical comparisons are $(b/a)/(c/d)\mapsto db/(ac)$ and $(n/a)/(c/d)\mapsto dn/(ac)$, with $a,d\in S$, $c\notin\mathfrak q$; their inverses are $b/c\mapsto(b/1)/(c/1)$ and $n/c\mapsto(n/1)/(c/1)$. Hence $T=B_{\mathfrak q}$ and $P=N_{\mathfrak q}$. On the other hand $\mathcal O_{S,t}=K$ with maximal ideal zero. Applying the fibre-stalk quotient lemma at $y$ gives $\mathcal O_{X_t,y}=\mathcal O_{X,y}$, and pullback on module stalks gives $(\mathcal F_t)_y=\mathcal F_y\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,y}}\mathcal O_{X,y}=\mathcal F_y$. Combining with step 6 gives the required generic-fibre identifications; all maps agree on germs and scalar fractions.

source.place: Tag 0GSI (lemma-associated-point-specializes), third proof paragraph, final generic-fibre localizations; schemes.tex Tag 0HA1 (lemma-local-ring-fibre); algebra.tex Tags 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization), 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization).

proof.text: By the definition of relative assassin, membership of $x$ (respectively $y$) is association of its unique point in $X_s$ (respectively $X_t$), and association means that the maximal ideal of the fibre local ring is the annihilator of some stalk element. The compatible isomorphisms of steps 3 and 7 send maximal ideals to maximal ideals and element annihilators to element annihilators: $a v=0$ if and only if its image scalar kills the image of $v$. They therefore give exactly $\mathfrak m_R\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(L)$ and $\mathfrak m_T\in\operatorname{Ass}_T(P)$, respectively.
